messages:
nina: FYI saw a spike of TLS handshake failures from eu-proxy -> ingress at 08:12 UTC. Quick glance shows proxies falling back to an old intermediate cert chain. KMS decrypt logs also show some unwrap errors. raising here for triage.
charles: can you paste the s_client output? wondering if it's SNI mismatch or stale certchain.
nina: pasted from a failing host:```
$ openssl s_client -connect ingress.eu.redwood:443 -servername api.redwood.test -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = OldCA, CN = Old Intermediate CA
verify error:num=10:certificate has expired
---
SSL handshake has read 1207 bytes and written 512 bytes
---
PDUs: TLSv1.2, Cipher is ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
```
ryan: hmm expired intermediate present. Wasn't there a rollout that swapped intermediates last week? Might be cert-provisioner cache still serving old chain during failover.
lena: I saw a config change on proxy-fleet-2 yesterday updating truststore order. could be the proxy sending chain in the wrong order (cert-shadowing).
charles: +1 to cache theory. Also KMS unwrap errors you mentioned, nina — any stack traces?
nina: KMS unwraps show "InvalidKeyMaterial" for some sessions, but only when clients fail to negotiate modern TLS (they fall back to older ciphers and the server side tries to unwrap with different CEK). snippet:```
2024-10-11T08:12:15Z ingress[proxy]: unwrap failed id=abc123 err=InvalidKeyMaterial
2024-10-11T08:12:16Z ingress[proxy]: tls handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate
```
sec-bot: Incident detected: tls-handshake-eu-2024-10-11. Paging oncall. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/tls-handshake-failures
sre-oncall: oncall here, I can take lead. Quick checklist: 1) verify which proxies are serving old chain (eu-proxy-1/2/3), 2) force cert-provisioner cache flush, 3) confirm KMS key version used for CEK unwrap, 4) enable verbose audit log for cert issuance.
charles: I'll run a one-off job to dump certchains from proxies and compare. command I'll use:```
for host in eu-proxy-{1..4}; do ssh $host "openssl s_client -connect localhost:8443 -showcerts" > /tmp/$host.chain; done
```
ryan: Regarding RBAC, cert-provisioner recently had a role tweak. if the provisioner lost permission to read the active KMS keyring, it might fallback to an older key. I opened a quick IAM check: https://console.iam/internal/policies/ctr-certer
lena: I can audit the proxy config push. If chain order got swapped at deploy-time the proxy will present intermediate first which can cause some clients to validate against the older root.
nina: Priority: high. Customer-facing retries observed for eu region. ETA on mitigations?
sre-oncall: immediate mitigation steps: (1) toggle proxy fleet to use pinned new chain (config flag) — revert if fails, (2) flush cert-provisioner cache and restart the service on eu-controlplane, (3) roll-forward KMS key version if unwrap errors persist, (4) upload full chain to central artifact repo and pin in proxies.
charles: After that, we should add an audit log entry for cert-chain changes and a smoke test to validate chain order post-deploy. We currently log cert issuance but not the presented chain order.
ryan: I'll add an RBAC follow-up: ensure cert-provisioner role has explicit kms:Decrypt on the active CEK key and a read-only binding to key metadata. filing ticket INFSEC-4123.
lena: I'll coordinate a quick canary deploy to eu-proxy-1 only, with increased tracing. Expect a 10min window to verify.
nina: thanks. For tracking: I've created minimal incident doc and linked artifacts in the runbook thread (internal link): https://redwood.incidents/2024/tls-eu-1723456789. Add any logs you gather.
sre-oncall: postmortem checklist: collect proxy certs, KMS unwrap traces, cert-provisioner audit logs, and RBAC policy change history. Also add a monitoring alert for any downgrade to TLSv1.2 with ECDHE-RSA ciphers in ingress.
charles: quick note — if we see "certificate has expired" in depth=2 consistently, we should run a sweep to detect any leftover bundles signed by OldCA across regions. I can script that.
ryan: action items summary: 1) charles — collect chains and run sweep (INFSEC-4124), 2) lena — proxy canary and config audit, 3) ryan — IAM check + ticket, 4) sre-oncall — execute immediate mitigations, 5) nina — incident doc + customer comms draft.
sec-bot: Acknowledged. Added labels [tls, eu, high-sev]. Next update in thread in 30m or on completion. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
